spec_match.rationale: Parses real strings through new URL() live, covers the space in host/path/query, the file:// exemption, the tab-stripped-before-parsing subtlety and the pipe control, and its edge-case suite states the spec expectation next to the observed behaviour — exactly the contract the Chrome 157 change is about.

interactive.rationale: A live input re-parses on every keystroke with component tiles and a contextual explanation, preset fill buttons cover the four interesting shapes, and the eight-case suite runs at load and on demand.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises typing any URL, watching new URL() take it apart or refuse it, plus a built-in edge-case suite — all delivered.

edge_cases.rationale: The both-worlds handling is exemplary on this pre-157 build: the observed 'Parsed' verdict is immediately annotated 'yet this browser parsed it — that is the pre-Chrome-157 behaviour', the suite highlights the two disagreeing rows, and the tab/LF/CR stripping distinction is demonstrated rather than asserted.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5083335148437504 and the forbidden-host-code-point spec section.

conformance.rationale: Seven of the eight feature assertions are contract-true and ran 6 pass / 2 fail on Chromium 141 (both space rejections failing is the correct pre-157 result) — but the percent-encoded-space-in-host-parses assertion appears to contradict the URL Standard for special schemes and is flagged for a human below.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): both the initial parse and the suite genuinely ran at load — console showed 'host=exa%20mple.com' for the space-in-host default and 'suite: 6/8 agree with the spec', matching the screenshots' red 'parsed' verdicts on the two space rows — while the fill buttons and manual typing were judged from wiring.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert fires url-parsed on every render and suite-run with the mismatch count (both observed at load); console carries only the page's labelled logs.

design_system.rationale: Layout and buttons follow the design system, but the emerald pass/parsed verdict text (--accent-emerald on stone/white, ~3.7-4.1:1) recurs here below WCAG AA for normal-size bold text; rose passes.

accessibility.rationale: The URL input is labelled, the suite summary is aria-live=polite, tables carry captions and header scoping, invisible code points are rendered as \xNN so rows stay readable, and verdicts pair icon with text.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at true 360px and 1280px: preset buttons wrap, component tiles stack, and the suite table stays inside the viewport because every cell allows overflow-wrap:anywhere — no horizontal overflow or clipped controls on either class.

openQuestions.title: FLAG FOR HUMAN: percent-encoded-space-in-host assertion looks wrong against the URL Standard
openQuestions.detail: conformance.json's 'percent-encoded-space-in-host-parses' asserts new URL('https://exa%20mple.com/').host === 'exa%20mple.com', citing the opaque-host parser. But https is a special scheme: the URL Standard's host parser percent-decodes the input first, and the decoded space is then a forbidden domain code point, so the spec (and its reference implementation, and Firefox/Safari behaviour) says this URL fails to parse. The assertion enshrines Chromium's legacy keep-%20 behaviour as the contract and will report a false failure on spec-conformant engines. The same claim is repeated in this page's suite row ('percent-encoded, a real host') and the feature index's API sample. Per the immutability rule I have not touched the assertion — a human should verify against WPT urltestdata and Chrome 157's actual behaviour and decide.

openQuestions.title: Emerald verdict text misses WCAG AA
openQuestions.detail: The .status.pass and td.verdict-pass emerald text sits at ~3.7-4.1:1 on its stone/white backgrounds, below the 4.5:1 requirement at these sizes. Recurring shared-palette finding across this review pass; one palette-level fix clears it.

summary: The strongest page in this feature: everything is measured live, and on this pre-157 Chromium 141 build the demo told the truth twice over — the default space-in-host URL parsed to host=exa%20mple.com with an amber note naming it the pre-Chrome-157 behaviour, and the auto-run suite reported 6/8 agreement with the two space rows highlighted red. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v157/disallow-spaces-in-non-file-url-hosts/host-parser/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots, DOM dump, clean console; feature /conformance/ route 6 pass / 2 fail as expected pre-157). The one substantive issue is not the page's behaviour but a contract question inherited from the suite: the %20-in-host row asserts Chromium's legacy parse as spec-correct, which the URL Standard appears to contradict — flagged for a human, not edited.
